purpose: Azelastine is used to relieve allergy symptoms like a runny or stuffy nose, sneezing, and itchy or watery eyes. It can help with seasonal allergies (like hay fever) as well as year-round allergies. There is also an eye drop form that helps with itchy, red eyes caused by allergies.
how_it_works: When your body encounters something you are allergic to, it releases a chemical called histamine, which causes all those uncomfortable allergy symptoms. Azelastine blocks the histamine from attaching to cells in your nose and eyes, which stops or reduces those symptoms. Think of it like putting a lock on a door so the histamine cannot get in and cause trouble.
common_side_effects: The most common side effect is a bitter or unpleasant taste in your mouth after using the nasal spray, which many people notice. You may also feel drowsy or tired, so be careful driving or operating machinery. Other possible side effects include headache, sneezing, nosebleeds, or a burning or stinging feeling in the nose or eyes.
warnings: Because azelastine can cause drowsiness, avoid drinking alcohol while using it, as that can make the sleepiness much worse. Be cautious driving or doing tasks that require alertness until you know how it affects you. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, breastfeeding, or taking other medications that cause drowsiness, such as sleep aids or anxiety medications. Keep the nasal spray away from your eyes unless you are using the specific eye drop form.
typical_dosing: For the nasal spray in adults and children 6 years and older, the usual dose is 1 to 2 sprays in each nostril twice a day. For the eye drops, the typical dose is 1 drop in each affected eye twice a day. Always follow the instructions your doctor or pharmacist gave you, and do not use more than directed.
